title: HelperSSHConnectionStateEvent
description: One observation of an ssh connection, sent to the coordinator that opened the pane riding it (nocx-oalo1.5.3, repaired by nocx-oalo1.5.3's review finding 6). It is a NOTIFICATION because a connection's state is revised for as long as the connection exists, in both directions, and there is no request to answer. `seq` orders observations of one connection WITHIN one helper instance; the coordinator fences it on the hello-ok instance id, because a connection id is a destination digest and outlives a helper replacement while sequences restart at 1. The shape is a oneOf per state, like the renderer's own pane.connection: each branch requires the fields its state makes true (a stage while opening, a person while waiting, a cause when failed, ended or reconnecting, an attempt while reconnecting) and forbids every field that state cannot own. A flat shape would admit `connected` with a stage and let a helper payload that satisfies this contract produce a renderer payload its stricter contract forbids. `plainShells` and the measurement (roundTripMs/slow) are optional on every state, because they are counts and measurements the supervisor carries beside the state.

oneOf.description: A dial in progress, at one of its stages.

connectionId.description: The supervisor's connection, the same value the `connection` op answered for the destination. A destination digest: it survives a helper replacement, which is why the sequence below is fenced by the source instance the coordinator stamps on delivery.

seq.description: Monotonic per connection for the life of ONE helper instance's supervisor. A receiver drops anything not greater than the last sequence it applied, and resets that sequence when the helper instance changes; that pair is how a late observation of an older moment is refused without refusing a replacement's first one.

stateMs.description: How long the connection has been in this state, at the observation, in milliseconds. The renderer ticks it locally from here, so a quiet connection costs no frames. Always present, including on a still-silent stalled connection whose measurement grew.

generation.description: Which LINK of the supervisor this observation is about: a monotonic identifier of the transport, not a count of links. It moves when a link is admitted and again when that link is retired or detached, so consecutive links do not have consecutive numbers — the first link is 1, its retirement 2, the second link 3 — and an observation taken while there is no link carries the number the retirement produced. Zero means no link has ever existed for this connection. Readers compare numbers (`!=`, `<`) and never read a value as an index. It is on the wire because it cannot be derived here: a `reconnecting` overtaken by `connected` arrives as one `connected`, so a coordinator that must drop what belongs to a link it has lost would otherwise be guessing.

stage.description: Where an opening is: resolve, tcp, ssh-version, key-exchange, sign-in, shell. REQUIRED while opening and forbidden on every other state — a stage on a connected connection is a fact that cannot exist.

plainShells.description: How many shells would end if this connection closed: its own, and those of everything dialed through it. Optional on every state because it is a count the supervisor carries, and a state that has none omits it (zero and absent are the same count).

roundTripMs.description: The newest probe's measurement, in milliseconds. Absent until a probe has answered; absent and zero are the same statement — nothing measured.

slow.description: Whether the backend GRADES that measurement slow. Sent rather than left to a reader to threshold, because the grade has hysteresis.
